title: KR21 European e-Books & e-Lending Community of Practice – Second Meeting
content:
When?

  • Date: 9 December 2026
  • Time: 11:00-12:30 CET

    • What?

    Established by the KR21 programme, the Community of Practice provides a space to share experiences, exchange knowledge, and collaborate on practical solutions to the legal, market, and technological challenges affecting e-Books and e-Lending. Read more about the Community.

    The Community builds on the principles set out in Safeguard Access, Empower Europe: An Action Plan to Let Libraries Be Libraries, and supports collective action to remove barriers that prevent libraries from fully delivering their public interest mission in the digital environment.

    Save Your Spot!

    Register now to secure your spot.

    The Webinar

    This second meeting will focus on trends in publisher licensing practices, exploring the different types of licences currently offered to libraries, what we can learn from them, and the potential red flags and challenges libraries should look out for when assessing or negotiating licence terms.

    We will hear from expert speakers bringing different perspectives to the topic, followed by an open discussion where everyone is welcome to share experiences, local initiatives and challenges.

title: Apply AI? It’ll Cost You
content:
Europe wants researchers and businesses to apply AI. But what happens when using AI on material they already have lawful access to means another licence, another payment, or a contractual ban?

Today, leaders from across Europe meet for the Apply AI Summit, a milestone in the EU’s wider efforts to encourage stronger uptake of AI across industrial sectors in Europe. It offers an opportunity to take stock of progress and set out plans on a topic that Commission President von der Leyen identified as a key priority in her State of the Union speech in September.

When the Apply AI Strategy first came out last year, Knowledge Rights 21 (KR21) welcomed it, recognising the value of an approach focused on the specific needs of each sector, rather than blunter, cross-cutting tools such as copyright. An untargeted approach risks causing significant collateral damage, in particular for research, and is not guaranteed to achieve its goals given that most (copyright-relevant) training takes place outside Europe.
